evidence_items.title: AI Day Gen 1 technical claims
evidence_items.claim: AI Day coverage reported early Optimus/Bumble C specs including about 73 kg weight, 2.3 kWh battery, 28 structural actuators, and 11 hand DoF.
evidence_items.notes: Presentation-reported specs, not current product specs; official event video improves provenance but not operational validation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: AI Day coverage reported battery, actuator, and hand figures.
evidence_items.source_location: Engineering.com AI Day technical summary; Tesla AI Day 2022 official event video
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official event source supports provenance; still not independently measured specs.

evidence_items.title: Untethered stage walking demo
evidence_items.claim: Optimus Gen 1 walked onstage and waved; a production-intent unit was shown on a stand and did not walk independently.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Ars reported one prototype walked and waved while another was rolled out on a stand.
evidence_items.source_location: Ars Technica AI Day demo report; Tesla AI Day 2022 official event video
evidence_items.verification_notes: Visible stage demo and official video provenance; no endurance/autonomy benchmark.

evidence_items.title: Curated manipulation and factory-like demo clips
evidence_items.claim: Tesla's AI Day 2022 presentation and contemporaneous reporting showed Bumble C/Optimus clips involving simple object handling, watering a plant, and moving metal parts, but reporting noted the clips were demo footage and at least some work was tethered rather than deployment proof.
evidence_items.notes: Useful as evidence of what Tesla chose to demonstrate, not as proof of robust autonomous work.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Small positive for existence of early manipulation demos; low confidence for autonomous task execution.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Reports describe demo footage of box handling, plant watering, and moving parts, with tethering caveats.
evidence_items.source_location: Tesla AI Day 2022 official video; Ars Technica and InsideEVs AI Day demo reports
evidence_items.verification_notes: No raw unedited task run, success rate, task duration, or intervention rate found.

evidence_items.title: Current Tesla page frames Optimus as a development goal
evidence_items.claim: Tesla's current AI & Robotics page describes creating a general-purpose, bipedal autonomous humanoid robot as the Optimus goal and recruiting need; it does not provide Gen 1 availability, deployment, benchmarks, or production-customer proof.
evidence_items.notes: Primary source for current product-status caution, not capability evidence.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supports keeping Gen 1 deployment and accessibility scores at zero.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Current Tesla page states the Optimus goal and hiring needs but no Gen 1 product availability.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Checked current official page during this update; no purchasable Gen 1 or customer deployment details found.

evidence_items.title: Later Optimus facility-task claims are not Gen 1 evidence
evidence_items.claim: Tesla's Q2 2024 update said Optimus was performing tasks or handling batteries in one of its facilities, but that statement postdates and does not identify the 2022 Gen 1 prototype; it should be excluded from Gen 1 scoring.
evidence_items.notes: This is negative/guardrail evidence for this robot record: do not transfer later Optimus claims to Gen 1.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Prevents current/later Optimus evidence from inflating historical Gen 1 scoring.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Tesla's 2024 update references Optimus facility tasks, not Gen 1.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Later company filing is credible for later Optimus context but not robot-specific proof for Gen 1.
